title: Open Checklist
description: A machine-readable aircraft checklist. One file describes the checklists for one aircraft type, variant, or individual airframe. Structure is semantic, not presentational: consumers decide layout.

open_checklist_version.description: Major.minor version of this schema the file targets. Consumers must refuse files with an unknown major version.

id.description: Stable, permanent identifier. Lowercase slug. Never reused for a different aircraft, never changed once published; the file may move but this id follows it.

title.description: Human-readable name for this checklist set, e.g. 'Cessna 172N Normal and Emergency Procedures'.

units.description: Units the numeric values in item text are expressed in. Stated explicitly because a mis-read unit is a safety defect.

speeds.description: Named reference speeds, in the unit given by units.airspeed. Optional, but strongly recommended: it lets software show V-speeds without parsing prose.

sections.description: The checklists themselves, in the order a pilot would normally encounter them.

extensions.description: Namespaced consumer-specific data. Keys must contain a dot-separated vendor prefix. Consumers must ignore unknown extensions; nothing safety-relevant may live here.

make.description: Manufacturer as it appears on the airworthiness paperwork or kit documentation, e.g. 'Cessna', 'U-Fly-It'.

variant.description: Series/variant suffix that changes procedures, e.g. 'N', 'S G1000'.

icao_type.description: ICAO aircraft type designator where one exists. Many ultralights have none; omit rather than invent.

category.description: Regulatory/operating category this file is written for. Drives how strictly the corpus treats the file.

airframe_specific.description: Set when this file documents one individual airframe rather than a type. Type-level files must omit it.

provenance.description: Where this content came from and who is answerable for it. Required: an unattributed checklist cannot be assessed for trustworthiness or for rights.

method.description: How the content got into this file. 'ocr_assisted' and 'ocr_raw' mean a machine read the source; both require review before the file may be trusted.

tool.description: Tool and version that produced the transcription, e.g. 'claude-opus-5'. Required for OCR methods so a systematic tool error can be traced and re-run.

converted_from.description: For method=format_conversion: the source format id, e.g. 'ace', 'gplt', 'fmd'.

contributors.description: People answerable for this file. At least one. A contributor's presence here asserts they accepted the contributor warranty in CONTRIBUTING.md.

contact.description: Email or URL. Optional, but a file with no reachable contributor cannot be a candidate for the highest verification states.

credentials.description: Free text, e.g. 'CFI', 'A&P', 'type owner since 2011'. Never treated as verified by the project.

source.description: The document this file was derived from. 'kind' drives the rights analysis, so it must be honest even when inconvenient.

kind.description: What class of document the content came from. 'none' means nothing was transcribed: the content is original work by the contributor.

pages.description: Page or section reference within the source, so a reviewer can find the same text.

allOf.comment: Anything transcribed from a real document must identify that document well enough for a reviewer to locate it.

verification.description: Trustworthiness of this file, on two independent axes. Neither axis implies the other: a file can be a faithful copy of a bad checklist, or a well-flown checklist that no longer matches its source.

source_fidelity.description: Does the content match the source document? unreviewed = nobody has checked machine or first-pass output. single_reviewed = one person other than the transcriber compared it line by line against the source. dual_reviewed = two independent people did, without seeing each other's result. not_applicable = there is no source document (authored content).

operational_review.description: Has this been exercised in the actual aircraft? none = never. ground_checked = walked through against the real cockpit, every control located and labelled as written. flown = flown behind in this type. Flying behind a checklist proves the items present are workable; it does NOT prove nothing is missing, so this axis can never substitute for source_fidelity.

completeness.description: Whether the file covers the source's full procedure set or only part of it. Partial files are legitimate but must say so, because a missing emergency section is invisible to a reader.

reviews.description: Individual review events. Each entry is a claim by a named person, recorded so it can be audited or withdrawn.

source_used.description: For source_comparison: which document the reviewer actually held. A review against a different revision than the transcriber used is a finding, not a pass.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of the file at review time. Lets tooling detect that content changed after the review and downgrade the state automatically.

known_issues.description: Open defects the contributors are aware of. A file with an unresolved safety_defect must not be presented as usable.

rights.description: Per-file rights. Deliberately per-file and not repo-wide: the project cannot grant a licence in text it does not own, so a blanket corpus licence would be a false statement for POH-derived files.

status.description: Rights posture for this file. public_domain = source carries no enforceable copyright (government work, or expired/forfeited). original_expression = wording is the contributor's own, expressing procedure taken as fact. upstream_reserved = wording is substantially the source's; the project asserts no licence and redistribution may be limited. unresolved = not yet analysed; must not be published.

corpus_license.description: SPDX identifier under which the project offers this file. Only meaningful when status is public_domain, original_expression, or licensed.

public_domain_basis.description: Why the source is public domain. Required when status is public_domain, so the claim can be checked rather than trusted.

permission_evidence_url.description: Link to written permission, where the rights rest on a grant from the holder.

redistribution.description: What the project believes downstream users may do. 'unrestricted' requires a status other than upstream_reserved.

section.description: One checklist, e.g. 'Before Start'. Bound to a phase id so software can map it to a moment in flight without parsing the title.

phase_label.description: Required when phase is 'other': the real name of the phase. Prevents 'other' becoming a dumping ground with no machine meaning.

criticality.description: Normal, abnormal, or emergency. Drives presentation and export grouping. Defaults to normal.

id.description: Stable identifier for this section within the file, for cross-references and deep links.

condition.description: When this checklist applies, e.g. 'Engine fire during start'. Meaningful mainly for abnormal and emergency sections.

phase.description: Controlled vocabulary of flight phases and abnormal situations. Stable ids: values are never renamed or removed, only added. Consumers must tolerate unknown values by treating them as 'other'.

item.description: One line of a checklist. Type determines whether it is a task at all: note, caution, warning and subtitle are information, not work, and cannot be ticked.

type.description: action = challenge with an expected response ('Fuel selector' / 'BOTH'). challenge = a task with no stated response. subtitle = a heading inside the checklist. note/caution/warning = information of increasing severity. reference = pointer to another checklist or document. blank = deliberate visual spacing, carried only for faithful reproduction.

text.description: The challenge, heading, or informational text. Required for every type except blank.

response.description: The expected response or state, conventionally upper case, e.g. 'BOTH', 'CHECK', 'FULL FORWARD'. Only meaningful for type=action.

id.description: Stable identifier within the section. Required for any item that is a memory item or a branch target, so references survive reordering.

tickable.description: Whether a consumer may present a checkbox. Derived from type and must not contradict it: information items are never tickable. Present so that consumers need no type table to behave safely.

memory_item.description: True when this action must be performed from memory before consulting the checklist. Safety-significant and lost by every vendor format, so it is first-class here.

indent.description: Nesting depth for sub-items, 0-4. Structural, not cosmetic: an indented item is subordinate to the preceding shallower item.

detail.description: Longer explanation shown on demand. Never required to complete the item; anything required belongs in text or response.

condition.description: Guard on this item, e.g. 'If equipped', 'Night only'.

value.description: Machine-readable form of a numeric response, so software can compare against sensed values instead of parsing prose.

reference.description: For type=reference: what to go to. section_id points inside this file; document/text point outside it.

source_confidence.description: Transcriber's or tool's confidence in this specific line. Set below 1.0 to flag a reading a reviewer must resolve; any item below the corpus threshold blocks promotion out of unreviewed.

allOf.comment: Everything except a deliberate blank must carry text.
A blank carries nothing else of substance.
Only an action has an expected response or a comparable value.
An action must state its expected response; that is what makes it an action rather than a challenge.
A warning is not a task. Information items and blanks can never be ticked, and can never be memory items.
Conversely, a real task is never marked untickable.
A reference item must say what it refers to.
A memory item must be addressable, so tooling and reviewers can refer to it stably.
